THE EPIC'S OWN INSTRUMENT, AUDITED BY ITS OWN LAW. Three defects in scripts/pds-ledger-census.sh, each measured this wave, each with its anti-pattern already identified. All three land in ONE file plus its selftest, so they are ONE slice — but they are three INDEPENDENT changes and each carries its own proof.

BASELINE, DRY-RUN AND CONFIRMED: bash scripts/pds-ledger-census_test.sh from a CLEAN directory is 80 checks, rc=0.
HAZARD, REPRODUCED TWICE: the census runs exec python3 - "$@", so sys.path[0] is '' = CWD, and bisect is a transitive stdlib import. A stray bisect.py in the working directory fails ALL 80 checks AND EXECUTES that file's top-level code — a real leftover bisect.py in a shared scratchpad issued live bp writes during a selftest run. RUN EVERY GATE FROM A CLEAN DIRECTORY.

────────── (1) CLAUSE 6 — THE CONTRADICTION THE INSTRUMENT CANNOT SEE ──────────
THIRTEEN closure rows are simultaneously lifecycle-claimable and disposition-closed. The census counts them in clause 4(a)'s numerator as SATISFIED, while bp task ready hands them to a worker. git show origin/main:api/lib/barkpark/tasks/queue.ex | grep -c disposition returns 0 — disposition is not a readiness axis — so NO instrument anywhere looks.
CLOSED-ONLY, AND THIS IS RULED, NOT OPTIONAL (PDS-D372, minted this wave). Implement it as clause 4(d)/6: ~12 lines — one comprehension over the already-computed live list, one additive JSON key (live_contradiction, a ROW-ID LIST not a count — 'a count nobody can turn back into rows is not a worklist'), one predicate line. MEASURED COST: the UNMODIFIED 80-check selftest still passes 80/80, including TERMDUP (which pins that clauses 1-3 stay closure-scoped) and every anchor fixture; and on the live board every existing figure is byte-identical, the only JSON delta being the new key.
PARKED-INCLUSIVE IS REFUSED ON THE RECORD AND YOU MUST NOT SHIP IT. Measured: extending the clause to parked FAILS 7 of 80 checks, and the FIRST failure is the CONTROL — build_healthy's kid-c is blocked parked and is inherited by all 34 fixture dirs. It also reds SHAREDTRIG, the fixture that exists specifically so 'no future wave can tighten clause 4' (PDS-D336(a)). And live, all 29 parked closure rows carry a STRUCTURED reopen_trigger — they are the epic's own exemplary shape. A live park awaiting its trigger is not a contradiction; it is a park.
THE VOCABULARY TRAP: match only the NORMALISED terms {open, closed, parked} and treat an unrecognised disposition as LIVE. Store-wide there are 41 off-vocabulary values, 26 of them tgw* rows carrying the literal 'open — demoted child of truth-grip-epic (charter D117)'. A rule phrased disposition IS NOT NULL AND != 'open' would silently delete 26 rows from a NEIGHBOUR EPIC's queue.
FAIL-BEFORE IS MANDATORY (PDS-D346): each new fixture must exit 0 against the UNMODIFIED origin/main census before it reds against yours. Build at least: a live+closed row on open (reds), a live+closed row on blocked (reds), a terminal+closed row (STAYS GREEN — otherwise you demand re-adjudicating history), a live PARK with a structured trigger (STAYS GREEN — this is the proof you did not ship the parked-inclusive form), and a --json check that the row-id list appears. Budget 80 -> ~85 checks.

────────── (2) --json IS NOT JSON WHEN IT CERTIFIES ──────────
REPRODUCED: bash c.sh --json --assert-round-done --anchor-from-paper pds-wave-27-2026-07-31 writes the JSON object and THEN the human ROUND-DONE PREDICATE block to the SAME stdout. jq -e . exits 5, 'Invalid numeric literal'. Source: the JSON is dumped around :905, then :926-996 print the predicate with bare print() and NO args.json guard. The script is careful everywhere else — die(), retry notices and the failure VERDICT all use file=sys.stderr — so this is ONE MISSED GUARD.
THE GREEN PATH IS POISONED TOO, which is the sharpest form of the finding: on the healthy fixture the run exits 0 AND jq still fails rc=5. The certificate is unpipeable EXACTLY WHEN IT CERTIFIES.
AND THE PAYLOAD CARRIES NO VERDICT AT ALL — only counts. So even a clean stream leaves a scripted consumer without a machine path. Fold round_done (bool) and round_done_failures (list) into the report AND route the human block to stderr. Both.
THE ANTI-PATTERN, PROVEN: DO NOT implement this by deferring the JSON emit until after the predicate is computed. On origin/main the CLAUSE 5 incoherence path (exit 4) runs AFTER the emit and therefore STILL prints valid JSON — measured rc=4, 985 bytes, jq_rc=0. A deferred-emit draft turned that into rc=4, 0 bytes, jq_rc=4 — a FRESH honesty regression inside the honesty fix. The predicate is a pure function of report: hoist it into one, call it BEFORE the emit, stash round_done into report, print once at the existing site, then write the human lines to stderr.
NO CONSUMER BLOCKS THIS: git grep -n -I -e 'assert-round-done' -e 'ROUND-DONE PREDICATE' -e 'VERDICT: ROUND' origin/main finds only the census, its selftest, charter prose, and two grip-ledger recipes that quote exit codes. Every selftest assertion captures 2>&1, so a stderr move costs ZERO test rewrites — verified by running the suite against a patched copy (80/80).

────────── (3) THE PAGED READ HAS NO STABLE ORDER ──────────
census.sh:387 sends limit=%d&offset=%d and NO order, so query.ex:704's catch-all applies desc: d.updated_at — a MUTATING sort key paged by explicit offset. A concurrent write teleports its row to index 0, shifting every row between; PROVEN live in six requests (the probe row at index 3 was NEVER SERVED, and offsets 0 and 1 both returned the same row).
THE SKIP IS NOT SILENT FOR WRITES — the shift produces a skip and a duplicate 1:1, and the duplicate detector exits 4 (proven on a fixture: rc=4, 'SNAPSHOT INCOHERENT: 1 row(s) were served on more than one page'). The genuinely silent variant is a concurrent DELETE, which shifts rows UP and produces no duplicate. Nothing detects that.
THE FIX IS A URL SUFFIX AND IT IS PROVEN IMMUNE: &order=_createdAt:asc. Measured on the live corpus — 3901 rows, ZERO _createdAt ties, globally sorted across four 1000-row pages; and write-immune: the probe sat at index 3894 BEFORE and AFTER a stage write, with byte-identical _createdAt and zero rows gained or lost, while the same write under the default order put that row at index 0.
TWO TRAPS, EACH ONE KEYSTROKE AWAY, EACH THIS EPIC'S OWN LIE CLASS LIVE IN THE ORDER PARAM:
  (a) order=doc_id (no direction) does NOT error — it fails query_controller.ex:706's <field>:(asc|desc) regex and SILENTLY falls back to updated_at DESC at HTTP 200. The response is byte-identical to sending no order. A 'fix' spelled this way is a green diff with ZERO behaviour change.
  (b) order=doc_id:asc parses as a CONTENT field and sorts jsonb_extract_path(content,'doc_id'), which is NULL for every task row — an all-NULL sort key is an UNSPECIFIED order that can skip and duplicate with NO concurrent write at all. Strictly worse than the bug.
ONLY _createdAt:asc IS CORRECT. Prove the spelling, do not assume it.

THE GREEN PATH IS POISONED TOO, which is the sharpest form of the finding: on the healthy fixture the run exits 0 AND jq still fails rc=5. The certificate is unpipeable EXACTLY WHEN IT CERTIFIES.
AND THE PAYLOAD CARRIES NO VERDICT AT ALL — only counts. So even a clean stream leaves a scripted consumer without a machine path. Fold `round_done` (bool) and `round_done_failures` (list) into the report AND route the human block to stderr. Both.
THE ANTI-PATTERN, PROVEN: DO NOT implement this by deferring the JSON emit until after the predicate is computed. On origin/main the CLAUSE 5 incoherence path (exit 4) runs AFTER the emit and therefore STILL prints valid JSON — measured rc=4, 985 bytes, jq_rc=0. A deferred-emit draft turned that into rc=4, 0 bytes, jq_rc=4 — a FRESH honesty regression inside the honesty fix. The predicate is a pure function of `report`: hoist it into one, call it BEFORE the emit, stash round_done into `report`, print once at the existing site, then write the human lines to stderr.
NO CONSUMER BLOCKS THIS: `git grep -n -I -e 'assert-round-done' -e 'ROUND-DONE PREDICATE' -e 'VERDICT: ROUND' origin/main` finds only the census, its selftest, charter prose, and two grip-ledger recipes that quote exit codes. Every selftest assertion captures 2>&1, so a stderr move costs ZERO test rewrites — verified by running the suite against a patched copy (80/80).

────────── (3) THE PAGED READ HAS NO STABLE ORDER ──────────
census.sh:387 sends `limit=%d&offset=%d` and NO order, so query.ex:704's catch-all applies `desc: d.updated_at` — a MUTATING sort key paged by explicit offset. A concurrent write teleports its row to index 0, shifting every row between; PROVEN live in six requests (the probe row at index 3 was NEVER SERVED, and offsets 0 and 1 both returned the same row).
THE SKIP IS NOT SILENT FOR WRITES — the shift produces a skip and a duplicate 1:1, and the duplicate detector exits 4 (proven on a fixture: rc=4, 'SNAPSHOT INCOHERENT: 1 row(s) were served on more than one page'). The genuinely silent variant is a concurrent DELETE, which shifts rows UP and produces no duplicate. Nothing detects that.
THE FIX IS A URL SUFFIX AND IT IS PROVEN IMMUNE: `&order=_createdAt:asc`. Measured on the live corpus — 3901 rows, ZERO _createdAt ties, globally sorted across four 1000-row pages; and write-immune: the probe sat at index 3894 BEFORE and AFTER a stage write, with byte-identical _createdAt and zero rows gained or lost, while the same write under the default order put that row at index 0.
TWO TRAPS, EACH ONE KEYSTROKE AWAY, EACH THIS EPIC'S OWN LIE CLASS LIVE IN THE ORDER PARAM:
  (a) `order=doc_id` (no direction) does NOT error — it fails query_controller.ex:706's `<field>:(asc|desc)` regex and SILENTLY falls back to updated_at DESC at HTTP 200. The response is byte-identical to sending no order. A 'fix' spelled this way is a green diff with ZERO behaviour change.
  (b) `order=doc_id:asc` parses as a CONTENT field and sorts jsonb_extract_path(content,'doc_id'), which is NULL for every task row — an all-NULL sort key is an UNSPECIFIED order that can skip and duplicate with NO concurrent write at all. Strictly worse than the bug.
ONLY `_createdAt:asc` IS CORRECT. Prove the spelling, do not assume it.

tags.rationale: The census is the PDS epic's own certifying instrument.
An instrument that cannot see a lie is the epic's own law broken.
Every new clause needs a fail-before fixture that reds on main first.
Stable paging is what makes the certified snapshot a snapshot.
It encodes PDS-D372 and refuses the parked-inclusive form on the record.

documents.title: The certifying instrument stops lying about itself: clause 6 counts the claimable-and-closed contradiction, --json becomes pipeable, and the paged read gets a stable total order
